newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seven firms supplied Saudi barley - traders.
newsitem.headline: Seven firms supplied Saudi barley - traders.

text.p: Around seven international grain firms were involved in selling one million tonnes of barley to Saudi Arabia in a deal confirmed on Thursday, traders said.
The major grain firm with the largest share of the deal appeared to be supplying around a quarter of a million tonnes, grain traders said.
The smallest single share of the deal was said to be 100,000 tonnes or less.

The deal was essentially the one which took shape on Wednesday after a tender the previous day, although there was some uncertainty over the precise range of prices. These were reported in a range of $142 to $148 per tonne including freight.
Traders said the low end of the range was $143 or more likely $142 per tonne and the high end was $147 or $148 per tonne for a total package worth over $140 million.
Saudi Arabia is the world's largest barley importer for its animal herds and tendered on Tuesday for a million tonnes of the grain with September and October arrival.
It buys around five million tonnes annually.
